workLog.step: Verified both review findings against the code before accepting either. The tight blockquote >/templates/agents/x.md returned 0 while the spaced form returned 1, and the old negative lookbehind returned 1 for both, so the anchor change had regressed it.

Measured the reviewer's other two suggestions rather than applying them. Building the anchor with a colon added makes C:\templates\agents\x.md and C:\.agents\specs\x.md count, because a drive letter is a colon followed by a single separator. Adding an equals sign makes the URL query parameter ?next=/.agents/x count. Each fixes one shape and breaks one, so only the blockquote marker was added.

Fixed the blockquoted fence. A fenced code block has no lazy continuation, so it ends with its blockquote, but the close test stripped the quote prefix from every later line without checking the quote was still open. An unquoted line inside a quoted fence and an unterminated quoted fence both swallowed real top-level prose, which is the dangerous direction for a gate.

Ended the fence when the blockquote ends and re-read that line at top level rather than consuming it, so a bare fence marker there opens the top-level fence it should. Without the re-read the shape flipped from a false negative to a false positive instead of being correct.

Added 10 tests: 1 anchor shape, 3 for the fence behavior, and 6 that pin the colon and equals trade so a future contributor who adds either character sees the casualties fail. Confirmed the 4 behavioral ones fail against origin/main's module and the 6 guards pass on both, because they document a deliberate limit rather than a change.

Corrected three stale test counts the review found in the merged PR's own documents. The session log gate said 93 passed and the decision memory said 55 to 93 and nineteen of 93. An earlier correction pass had fixed only the workLog and the episode.

Adversarial review on gpt-5.6-sol falsified this PR's central design claim. The PR asserted that admitting a colon or an equals sign to the anchor set trades one false negative for one false positive, so neither is a net gain, and pinned that assertion with three tests asserting false negatives. The review supplied a contextual formulation and a nine-shape matrix showing the trade is not forced.

Verified the reviewer's premise independently before complying, rather than accepting the verdict. Ran the nine-shape matrix against this branch's module: naming the two contexts, a label or link-reference-definition colon and an HTML attribute equals, counts all three shapes the raw characters would reach and admits none of the six that the raw characters would wrongly count. 9 of 9 correct.

Replaced the raw-character trade with two named context anchors. _LABEL_ANCHOR requires the label itself to sit at an anchor, which is what keeps a Windows drive letter and a colon inside a URL out. _ATTR_ANCHOR requires an enclosing tag and a real attribute name, which is what keeps a URL query parameter out. Rewrote the three tests that pinned the false negatives and extended the negative control from three shapes to six.

Fixed a second defect the review found with two CommonMark cross-checks: the quoted-fence state recorded only a boolean, so a depth-2 marker closed a depth-1 fence, exposing code as prose, and a fence opened at depth 2 survived a drop to depth 1, hiding real prose. Replaced the boolean with the opening depth and added helpers that count markers and strip exactly the opening depth.

Measured the result: 112 tests pass on the branch. Against the module on origin/main, 9 of those 112 fail, and each maps to a specific defect: 1 for the tight blockquote anchor, 3 for the labelled and attribute contexts, 3 for the quoted-fence lifecycle, 2 for the depth tracking. The corpus scan reports no drift, so the widened anchors catch nothing new in the shipped skills.

Corrected two documents that pinned a historical reproduction to origin/main, a moving target. main has since absorbed PR #3472, so the documented command now reports 96 passed and proves nothing. Both now pin to 303f918ea, and the reproduction was re-run there to confirm the recorded 22 failed and 74 passed.

Declined the review's third finding rather than patching it. An indented code block inside a blockquote is still counted as prose. This is the fourth defect found in _strip_code across two PRs, and each fix has been one more special case in a hand-rolled block parser. markdown-it-py is already a direct dependency and scripts/utils/markdown_parser.py already wraps it, so the remedy is to walk the AST instead. Filed as #3499 rather than mixing a rewrite into a behavior fix.
